answer: An operator running many aliases therefore pays for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the ivory quota and the gale admission check. Because the counters live in the copper ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. Submission rate is limited to 5 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole fleet from one uplink. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
